Key visual features: Large, dark brown/black angular necrotic lesion on the upper leaf surface with yellow halo around it, leaf appears tattered with a hole where tissue has fallen out. Scattered small yellow spots visible elsewhere on the leaf.

Top candidates: **Bacterial_Blight** (angular lesions with yellow halo, tattered/falling-out centers), **Septoria_brown_spot** (dark brown lesions, yellowing), **Bacterial_Pustule** (irregularly shaped areas with yellow halo).

Let me view reference images for these candidates.

The Bacterial_Blight reference shows early-stage small scattered spots, not the large consolidated lesion in the test image. Let me check Anthracnose which causes "irregularly shaped red to dark brown blotches."

Anthracnose shows late-season pod/stem symptoms - doesn't match the leaf lesion in the test image.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: Large, dark brown/black irregular necrotic lesion on upper leaf surface with yellow-green halo
- Hole/tattered appearance where lesion tissue has fallen out
- Scattered small yellow spots on the rest of the leaf (early-stage lesions)

This matches **Bacterial_Blight** description: "angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered." The reference images show early-stage disease, while the test image shows advanced coalesced lesions - consistent with the described disease progression.
